title: Decide durability and replication once in the dispatch wrapper, not per handler
description:
The RPC dispatch table had 102 arms and none of them marked the auto-save manager, so writes made over RPC were skipped by the periodic compaction loop (it only runs when changes are pending) and lost on a hard kill. The REST handlers call mark_changed() in 15 separate places, which is exactly why RPC's omission went unnoticed: the obligation lives in each handler, so a new handler silently opts out.

The fix wraps the command table instead of editing every arm: dispatch() calls dispatch_authenticated(), then consults a single command_mutates(&str) classifier and, on a successful reply, marks auto-save and replicates. Adding a command means adding one row to that classifier, and two unit tests assert the classifier covers every write and excludes every read.

Two details that made the wrapper work without cost:
- Replication needs the target collection after args are consumed, but cloning args would copy multi-megabyte payload frames. Copy only the two leading string arguments (every mutating command carries the collection there), and take vector ids from the handler's reply instead of the request — which also fixes server-generated ids and partly-failed batches, since a batch reply marks each row's status.
- The wrapper reads response.result.is_ok(), so a refused command never marks anything dirty.
whenToUse: Adding a cross-cutting obligation (durability, replication, audit, metrics) to a large command/route table where per-handler calls would be forgettable.
